This article tries to clarify the more obscure aspects of ariadne by answering
questions from the community, myself included.

# Questions & Answers

**How does ariadne fetch online resources?**

Great question! In general, ariadne combines four different resource types:

- Zenodo records
- Online file directories (FTP)
- SPARQL endpoints
- RESTful APIs

For example, ChocoPhlAn, GO, UniProt and KEGG are fetched from
[this Zenodo record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17100033),
[this FTP folder](https://current.geneontology.org/),
[this SPARQL endpoint](https://sparql.uniprot.org/) and
[this API endpoint](https://www.kegg.jp/kegg/rest/keggapi.html), respectively.

**Can I extend the ariadne graph with custom resources?**

You can add custom single linkmaps (both local and remote) to the ariadne graph
with `addResource()`. If you believe a key resource is missing, you can let us
know by opening a _resource request_ issue
[here](https://github.com/Minotau-R/ariadne/issues).

**Can I access a previous resource version?**

Yes, for example you can point to past BugSigDB and WoL releases with
`ariadne(versions = list(BugSigDB = "v1.2.2", WoL = "v20April2021"))`. Available
resources and their versions can be listed with `listResources()` and
`listResourceVersions()`, respectively.

**How does ariadne handle multiple resource versions?**

The [Zenodo record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23584782) of the ariadneDB 
contains `gml` files each describing one resource. As long as the network
structure of a resource (links between features) stay the same, that resource is
encoded by the latest ariadneDB release. When a resource structure changes (any
link between two features is added and/or removed), all versions up to that
point are fixed to that moment's ariadneDB release, while new versions are
encoded by the latest ariadneDB release.

**How can a single ariadneDB release encode multiple versions of a resource?**

Even if a resource size changes over time, the links between its features are
likely to be much more stable. All that matters to ariadne is the network
structure of a resource, that is, how their features link to each other. For
simplicity, you can can think of the different `gml` files as mere templates for
the resource network structures.

With that said, every time `ariadne()` is run, the URL links to the resources
are updated based on the requested resource versions (in practice, for each
resource the `"{version}"` placeholder is replaced with the requested version).

An important caveat is that only file-based resources (Zenodo records and online
file directories) allow access to past resource releases, whereas SPARQL
endpoints and APIs always point to the current release.
